name: Apoptosis — extrinsic (death-receptor) pathway
summary: Death ligands (FasL, TRAIL) on immune cells cluster death receptors on the target cell, assembling the DISC in which caspase-8 is activated. Caspase-8 directly activates caspase-3 (type I cells) and cleaves BID to engage mitochondria (type II cells).
clinical: Cytotoxic T cells and NK cells kill targets partly via FasL/TRAIL. FAS mutations cause ALPS. c-FLIP overexpression blocks DISC signalling in some tumours.

references.label: Reactome: Extrinsic Pathway of Fas/FasL-mediated apoptosis

nodes.label: c-FLIP
nodes.description: Catalytically inactive caspase-8 homologue that modulates DISC activity.

steps.title: 1 · Death ligand
steps.text: Trimeric FasL on a cytotoxic lymphocyte clusters Fas receptors on the target cell.

steps.title: 2 · DISC assembly
steps.text: Receptor death domains recruit FADD, whose death-effector domain recruits procaspase-8. c-FLIP can compete and blunt activation.

steps.title: 3 · Caspase-8
steps.text: Clustering forces procaspase-8 molecules together; they dimerise and auto-process into active caspase-8.

steps.title: 4 · Two routes to caspase-3
steps.text: In type I cells caspase-8 activates caspase-3 directly. In type II cells, caspase-8 cleaves BID; tBID activates BAX/BAK to engage the mitochondrial pathway as an amplifier.
